sections.heading: 2. Core Shona Grammar Rules Consolidated
points: Talking About the Past ('rakaiswawo'): Recent Today Past: [nda- / wa- / ta- / va-] + verb | Earlier Past: [ndaka- / waka- / taka- / vaka-] + verb
Colours & Describing Objects in Shona ('mutema'): Core Colours: -chena (white), -tema / nhema (black), -tsvuku (red) | Phrase pattern: ruvara rwe-[colour] (e.g., ruvara rwegirinhi)
Talking About the Past ('yakachenuruka'): Recent Today Past: [nda- / wa- / ta- / va-] + verb | Earlier Past: [ndaka- / waka- / taka- / vaka-] + verb

sections.heading: 3. Cultural Context & Practical Usage
points: Cold Drinks ('Zvinwiwa'), Mazoe Orange Crush & Afternoon Hospitality: On warm afternoons in Zimbabwe, welcoming a guest to the table with a cold glass of cordial—most famously Zimbabwe's iconic Mazoe Orange Crush diluted with chilled water and ice cubes ('magodo echando' from the 'firiji')—or a bottled soft drink ('chigubhu chedhiringi') is a beloved tradition of home hospitality..

Homestead Garden Tools ('Maturusi') & Local Blacksmith Craftsmanship: Every rural and suburban household in Zimbabwe keeps a set of sturdy hand tools—hoes ('mabadza'), rakes ('mahara'), digging forks ('mafoko'), and shovels ('mafoshoro')—fitted with carved hardwood handles ('mibato yemuti') to prepare vegetable beds and clear stony yard paths..

Veranda Container Gardening & Ornamental Plants in Zimbabwe: Container gardening—planting ornamental foliage and flowers ('maruva') in painted pots and tins ('magaba') arranged along smooth cement verandas ('pamusoro peuriri hwesimende')—is a cherished tradition in Zimbabwean homes, bringing greenery right to the doorstep even during the dry season..

Household Wares Markets & Woven Carrier Bags ('Mashangani'): At bustling community markets, vendors spread out practical household goods—sun hats, clothes pegs ('mapegisi'), scrubbing brushes ('mabhurashi'), and basins.

review_exercises.prompt: Review 11 — Folktales ('Ngano'): Who are the two classic characters in grandmother's fireside folktales ('ngano yetsuro negudo')?
options: The clever hare ('tsuro') and the baboon ('gudo')
review_exercises.correct_answer: The clever hare ('tsuro') and the baboon ('gudo')
review_exercises.explanation: 'Tsuro' (hare) and 'Gudo' (baboon) are the most famous duo in Shona 'ngano' storytelling.

review_exercises.prompt: Review 11 — Village Governance: What was the role of the traditional village council ('dare' / 'padare')?
options: Settling community disputes ('kutonga mhosva') and mentoring young men in good customs ('tsika')
herding cattle in the mountains at night
review_exercises.correct_answer: Settling community disputes ('kutonga mhosva') and mentoring young men in good customs ('tsika')
review_exercises.explanation: At the 'dare', elders adjudicated cases fairly and taught youth community values.

review_exercises.prompt: Review 11 — Figurative Language: What does the pair 'zvirevo nemadimikira' mean in English?
Review 11 — Passive Habitual ('-ai-...-wa'): In 'Nziyo dzechinyakare dzayiimbwa panguva dzekukohwa', what does 'dzayiimbwa' mean?
review_exercises.explanation: 'Dza-yi-imb-wa' combines Class 10 'dza-', habitual '-yi-/-ai-', verb '-imba' (sing), and passive '-wa' ('used to be sung').

review_exercises.prompt: Review 11 — Indigenous Crops: Which two traditional grains did people cultivate long ago before maize ('chibage')?
review_exercises.explanation: 'Mapfunde' (sorghum) and 'zviyo' (finger millet) are Zimbabwe's ancient drought-resistant staple grains.

review_exercises.prompt: Review 11 — Translate this new review sentence: 'Ambuya vaitaurira vazukuru vavo ngano dzinonakidza manheru.'
options: The teacher asked the students to write a short essay today.
Men used to forge iron spears and hoes in the village.
Grandmother used to tell her grandchildren delightful folktales in the evening.
The river is full of water after yesterday's heavy rain.
review_exercises.correct_answer: Grandmother used to tell her grandchildren delightful folktales in the evening.
review_exercises.explanation: 'Ambuya vaitaurira' = 'Grandmother used to tell', 'vazukuru vavo' = 'her grandchildren', 'ngano dzinonakidza manheru' = 'delightful folktales in the evening'.
